evidence.ref: build_notice in .warp/request_doorbell.py is a PURE function warp.request/v1 -> (notice_text, jira_link): it assembles a concise notice carrying a title ('[Doorbell] <touchpoint>: a decision is needed'), the tier ('Tier <tier>'), a one-line what (_what maps each touchpoint to a plain-words line), and the tracker link from record.tracker.url, and returns (None, None) when the request has no tracker link yet so the caller SKIPS it (nothing to link to), not errored. It is a SIGNAL only: the notice points at the tracker where the decision is made and recorded ('Decide in the tracker (the decision is made and recorded there): <link>'), carries NO approve/decide action, and the module has NO inbound path at all - there is no code that reads a reply as a decision (Telegram is the doorbell; the decision lives in the tracker, the W3 Decision issue). ring/ring_all read the record read-only (record.get(...)) and write nothing back into it or to disk.

scripts/selftest.py WARP-0618 block, offline (no network) over the FakeSink: each of the six touchpoints rings exactly one signal-only notice keyed 'REQ-<tp>:needs_decision' carrying '[Doorbell]', 'Tier standard', the touchpoint's one-line what (RD._what), 'Decide in the tracker', and the tracker link; the doorbell rings once per new request (notified 6, suppressed/skipped/failed 0); the notice carries no approve/reply-with-a-decision call to action; a request with no tracker link is SKIPPED (outcome skipped, nothing sent), not errored; and the request records are byte-unchanged after a run (json.dumps identical) - it reads read-only and writes nothing back. The send is an INJECTED sink seam (ring(record, sink, terms) calls sink.send(text, link, key=key)), reference-wired exactly like the W3 projection injects the live tracker adapter: the gate drives a deterministic in-module FakeSink (pure Python, no network) and the real TelegramSink is a reference implementation that resolves a SECRET-REFERENCE bot token at the seam (token_ref, e.g. env:TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, via the lazily-loaded shipped tracker_intake._default_secret_resolver, never a raw credential) and FAILS CLOSED (DoorbellError) with no token; it uses stdlib urllib against the Telegram Bot API and is NEVER constructed or run in the gate (the FakeSink is what runs there). FAIL-SAFE: ring wraps sink.send in try/except Exception and, on a delivery failure, returns outcome 'failed' with the error string, NEVER raising into the caller - a doorbell that cannot deliver must not block or advance a request; the request is untouched (the record dict is byte-identical after a failed send). ring_all is fail-safe end to end: one request's failure never stops the rest.

scripts/selftest.py WARP-0618 block: a FailingSink (send always raises RuntimeError) driven through ring returns outcome 'failed' with an 'error' key and attempts == 1, and the request record is byte-unchanged (json.dumps identical) - the error is swallowed, never raised. Tooth T2 proves the fail-safe wrap is load-bearing (below). The module selfcheck (python3 .warp/request_doorbell.py selfcheck) drives the fixture end to end over the FakeSink offline including the swallowed-failure case. Part of selftest 2544 passed, 0 failed.

IDEMPOTENT per (request_id, status): notice_key(record) is '<id>:<status>', and ring hands that key to the sink, which is keyed-idempotent like FakeTracker.comment - a chat channel gives NO read-back (the Telegram Bot API exposes no history), so the delivery channel owns the 'already rung' marker keyed by request+status: a keyed send delivers AT MOST ONCE per key (a repeat returns False, no delivery), so a re-run or a re-projection at the same status is suppressed and a genuine status change is a new key that rings again. No second offset ledger (the reconciler posture). REDACTED (RULE #3): build_notice passes the whole notice through redact(body, terms) - REUSED verbatim from .warp/request_projection.py (redact + _safe, never re-implemented) - before it is returned, so every secret reference (env:/keychain:) and every org-declared operating term (the injected declared terms) is masked to [redacted]; the tracker link is _safe'd and dropped fail-closed if a residue still matches a secret scheme (which skips the request). No secret reference or declared operating datum can reach the chat channel.

scripts/selftest.py WARP-0618 block: a re-run of all six requests at the same status is fully suppressed (suppressed 6, notified 0) and the sink is byte-stable; the same requests at a changed status (changes_requested) all ring again (notified 6, sink grows by six); a decision_choice request whose bound_artifact.ref carries a secret reference (env:PROD_DB_PASSWORD) and a declared operating datum (MRR 45000, passed as terms) projects a notice with BOTH masked and NEVER in the clear ('[redacted]' present) while the tracker link is preserved clean. THE SEND IS AN INJECTED REFERENCE SEAM NEVER GATE-RUN: ring takes the sink as a parameter; the gate drives the deterministic FakeSink (pure Python, no network). Idempotency is keyed by (request_id, status): because a chat channel gives no read-back, the marker lives with the delivery channel (the FakeSink models it as a keyed set; a real deployment pairs the send with a durable keyed marker the adopter wires, or drives it only from the reconciler). The tracker link is _safe'd (dropped fail-closed if a residue still matches a secret scheme, which skips the request), and the WHOLE notice passes through redact before it is returned - secret-reference schemes (env:/keychain:) always masked, org-declared operating terms masked case-insensitively (DECLARED per RULE #3, passed in as terms, not heuristically detected).
